headline: Skydance mandates five-day office week, offers voluntary buyouts to employees
summary: Following its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, Skydance is implementing a mandatory five-day in-office work policy and offering voluntary buyouts to eligible employees. Led by co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz, the post-merger directives aim to align workplace policies and achieve at least $2 billion in cost savings to address nearly $90 billion in debt. The new RTO mandate replaces a previous three-day hybrid model and will be phased in across major global offices.

headline: ArcelorMittal GBT appoints Preethi Panasa as head-HR operations
summary: ArcelorMittal Global Business & Technologies has appointed Preethi Panasa as its new head of HR operations. Bringing over 24 years of experience from leadership roles at organizations including GMR Group, Parexel, and Deloitte, she will focus on strengthening HR service delivery, process optimization, and technology-driven transformation.

headline: GitLab plans first India office in Bengaluru, looks to expand workforce
summary: US-based software platform GitLab plans to open its first physical office in India, selecting Bengaluru to expand its engineering, sales, and administrative workforce. The move represents a shift from its traditional remote-first model following a global restructuring that saw the company exit 22 countries to concentrate resources in high-growth talent hubs. The expanded Indian operations are positioned to support GitLab's core DevSecOps platform and its growing focus on AI-assisted software development.

headline: India’s GCCs to add up to 1.4 million net jobs by 2031: Report
summary: India's Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are projected to add up to 1.4 million net jobs by 2031, expanding their total workforce to nearly 3.7 million. Growth will be driven by multinational firms broadening their mandates into specialized fields like AI and cybersecurity, offsetting routine job losses from automation. Additionally, this expansion is expected to generate demand for 150 million to 170 million square feet of new office space, predominantly in Tier 1 cities.

headline: Servotech appoints Shivinder Singh Buttar as VP and head of HR
summary: Servotech Renewable Power System has appointed Shivinder Singh Buttar as Vice President and Head of Human Resources, effective September 2026. Bringing over 20 years of experience across the renewable energy, automotive, and manufacturing sectors, Buttar will lead Servotech's global HR strategy, workforce planning, and organizational development. His extensive background includes previous HR leadership roles at INA Solar, Future Solar, Sterlite Technologies, Volkswagen India, and Škoda Auto India.

headline: Saudi Arabia to raise wage threshold for Saudisation to SR6,000 by 2028
summary: Saudi Arabia will progressively increase the minimum monthly salary required for citizens to count fully toward private-sector Saudisation quotas under its Nitaqat programme. The threshold will rise to SR5,000 in April 2027 and SR6,000 in April 2028. While the policy does not mandate direct wage hikes, employers must adjust workforce planning to maintain compliance with nationalisation targets.

headline: Microsoft’s voluntary-exit offer to 60,000 employees, including India team
summary: Microsoft has launched a voluntary-exit program targeting approximately 60,000 employees globally across key divisions including AI, finance, and Xbox. Eligible staff up to the vice-president level have until December to decide on buyout offers, which include severance packages ranging up to a year's pay. The initiative aims to manage operational costs as the company scales up its capital expenditure for AI infrastructure.

headline: For TELUS Digital, the diversity question is no longer how many but where
summary: TELUS Digital is shifting its gender diversity strategy from tracking total headcounts to analyzing where women are positioned within the company's hierarchy and functions. By focusing on early management promotions, P&L exposure, and executive sponsorship, the firm aims to build a more equitable leadership pipeline.

headline: Embassy Group staff to go on 9-Day Diwali break
summary: Indian real estate developer Embassy Group has announced a nine-day company-wide break from November 7 to November 15, 2026, allowing employees to celebrate Diwali with their families. This 20-year annual tradition is part of the firm's broader employee well-being strategy, which also includes health initiatives, fitness perks, and leadership engagement platforms.

headline: Swiggy continues to support delivery partners with financial protection
summary: Indian on-demand convenience platform Swiggy has renewed its comprehensive insurance program for over 2.5 million delivery partners, offering coverage for accidental death, hospitalization, and maternity care. The updated policy covers pre-existing conditions from day one and includes additional benefits such as free teleconsultations, OPD support, and child education assistance. Swiggy also plans to expand its city-wide health check-up camps as part of its ongoing support for gig workers.

headline: Tata Elxsi to restructure work allocation as it targets higher productivity
summary: Tata Elxsi plans to shift select responsibilities from senior employees to trained junior staff over the next six months to boost workforce utilization from 78% and improve margins. Following the completion of its annual salary revisions, the company aims to keep employee costs stable through operational efficiencies. Additionally, Tata Elxsi remains focused on retaining specialized talent in high-demand areas such as engineering research and development.

headline: Generali to cut 9% of German workforce, consolidate offices
summary: Italian insurer Generali plans to reduce its German workforce by approximately 9%, primarily relying on voluntary retirement arrangements to achieve the cuts. As part of a broader operational streamlining effort, the company will also consolidate its country-wide office network into five main regional hubs.

headline: MCL appoints Rekha Pandey as director-HR
summary: Mahanadi Coalfields has appointed Rekha Pandey as its new Director of Human Resources. Bringing over 32 years of coal sector experience in HR and industrial relations, Pandey previously served in key managerial roles at Coal India and Central Coalfields Limited. In her new post, she will lead workforce management, personnel administration, and employee welfare initiatives for the public sector company.

headline: Essar Power appoints Soumiya Venkateswaran as head-HR
summary: Essar Power has appointed Soumiya Venkateswaran as its new Head of Human Resources. Venkateswaran brings over 20 years of strategic HR experience, having previously held senior leadership roles at Axis Bank, WNS Global Services, and Jet Airways. In her new position, she will lead Essar Power's workforce planning, talent management, and employee engagement strategies.

headline: Parachute Advansed Gold brings girlhood memories into new campaign
summary: Marico's Parachute Advansed Gold has launched a new marketing campaign titled 'Feel Like a Girl Again,' aimed at building an emotional connection with consumers through themes of nostalgia and female friendship. Conceptualized by Kakkoii Entertainment and directed by Gautham Vasudev Menon, the strategy shifts away from traditional problem-solution advertising toward positive emotional reinforcement. The campaign will roll out across television, cinema, and digital platforms.

headline: JioHotstar launches StreamToCart Ads with Instamart
summary: JioHotstar has introduced StreamToCart Ads in partnership with quick-commerce platform Instamart, allowing viewers to browse and add products to their carts without interrupting video playback. The new shoppable ad format bridges upper-funnel video advertising with direct e-commerce conversions, enabling brands to track real-time add-to-cart metrics. The feature leverages Instamart's commerce infrastructure to capitalize on the growing demand for quick-commerce services in India.

headline: Prabhakaran Thanraj to lead ICC Communications function
summary: Prabhakaran Thanraj, Vice President of Marketing and Business Development at the International Cricket Council (ICC), has been appointed to lead the organization's communications function in addition to his current duties. The consolidated leadership role aims to closely integrate marketing, communications, commercial strategy, and fan experience to drive global growth and new commercial initiatives. Thanraj previously held executive commercial and marketing roles at the Asian Cricket Council, the Board of Control for Cricket in India, and IMG.

headline: Pee Safe asks women to prioritise comfort during periods
summary: Pee Safe has launched a new brand campaign titled 'In Your Comfort Zone, Nothing Is Too Much,' which encourages women to prioritize personal comfort over routine management during their periods. Reversing the popular phrase that growth happens outside one's comfort zone, the campaign highlights the features of its overnight night pads designed for heavy flows. Ultimately, the initiative seeks to shift the period care narrative by framing comfort as an intentional choice rather than a secondary concern.

headline: Blue Buzz wins PR mandate for Yellowstone International Film Festival
summary: Public relations agency Blue Buzz has secured the integrated communications and PR mandate for the upcoming Yellowstone International Film Festival in Mumbai. Taking place from November 30 to December 4, the five-day event will showcase independent films, panel discussions, and masterclasses. Blue Buzz will lead the festival's media relations, strategic communication, and digital PR efforts to expand its reach.

headline: Mentos Fresh Action unveils new TVC built around a burst of freshness
summary: Perfetti Van Melle has launched a new television commercial for its recently introduced Mentos Fresh Action candy. The humorous campaign utilizes visual exaggeration to demonstrate the product's intense cooling freshness and engage young consumers. By leveraging a playful narrative, the company aims to highlight the expanding Mentos portfolio in India.

headline: SPNI launches Sony VIZHA in Malaysia on Astro
summary: Sony Pictures Networks India (SPNI) has launched Sony VIZHA, a new Tamil general entertainment channel, in Malaysia through pay-TV operator Astro. Marking SPNI's first linear channel debut on Astro, the service features a mix of reality formats, original fiction, and films with English subtitles. The strategic partnership expands SPNI's international footprint to reach Tamil-speaking audiences beyond India.

headline:
Smartphone
and earbud makers import more components from Vietnam as domestic prices surge
summary: Rising component costs and surging memory chip prices have led smartphone and earbud manufacturers in India to increase imports from Vietnam. Companies are leveraging zero-duty tariffs under the India-ASEAN Free Trade Agreement to import components rather than building local manufacturing facilities. This growing supply chain shift undermines India's domestic manufacturing incentive schemes and reduces government customs revenue.
